claims.statement: For finite positive generalized-polynomial rates rho_e=P_e/Q_e with finite rational supports and strictly positive coefficients, clearing D=product_e Q_e gives lifted channel support A_e+sum_{f!=e}B_f, whose directional maximum is h_D(w)+tau_e(w), where tau_e=h_{A_e}-h_{B_e}. Thus denominator clearing preserves every cross-channel score ordering and exact tie, including after excluding neutral arrows before taking the maximum.
assumptions: Every numerator and denominator support is finite and nonempty
Every listed coefficient is strictly positive
Exponents and reaction vectors are represented exactly
The essential-source convention removes nu_e dot w = 0 before taking the top score
claims.novelty_boundary: The support-function identity is elementary and internally proved here. No historical novelty or external review is claimed.
claims.costs: Structural recognition scans sparse supports and exact rational vectors. Explicit denominator lifting can create sum_e |A_e| product_{f!=e}|B_f| source tuples. Coefficient bit lengths are charged for exact positive-sign validation but do not affect tau.
claims.falsifier: A positive-coefficient finite input where product support height differs from the Minkowski-sum support identity, or a tied leading term cancels despite all coefficients being positive.
claims.next_gate: Independent check of the positive-tie factorization for generalized rational exponents and a library-level exact support representation.

claims.statement: For explicit sparse positive rational generalized-polynomial channel inputs with exact rational reaction vectors, NON-ENDOTACTIC is NP-complete and ENDOTACTIC is coNP-complete under the essential-source, exact-tie rule. Non-endotactic instances have polynomial-bit rational counterdirections. coNP-hardness holds with positive integer-polynomial numerators and denominators, coefficient 1, at most three monomials per side per channel, and O(1)-bit exponents/jumps in a dimension-varying sparse encoding.
assumptions: A direction is a real vector w in a dimension that is part of the input
tau_e(w)=max_{a in A_e} a dot w - max_{b in B_e} b dot w
Neutral channels are excluded before the active maximum
Every active channel tied at the maximum must point strictly inward
3SAT clauses may be restricted to three distinct variables
claims.novelty_boundary: The reduction and certificate-size proof are original internal work and have not been externally reviewed. Prior art includes MILP recognition for finite graph-based chemical networks; exact complexity of this rational sparse-support criterion was not found in the targeted search. No priority claim is made.
claims.costs: Reduction size O(n+m) channels, dimension n+1, at most three terms in each support; listed sparse exponents have constant magnitude. A direction certificate is checked in O(d times total support terms) exact rational dot-product work, with coefficient bit growth polynomial in the explicit input length.
claims.falsifier: A gap in the all-directions UNSAT implication in the 3SAT reduction, especially the neutral-clause average step for z>0, or the z=0 and z<0 slices; or a real non-endotactic instance for which every rational direction certificate misses the exact active maximum.
claims.next_gate: Independent expert proof review of the reduction and the rational basic-solution size argument; focused prior-art check on rational-rate structural recognition.

claims.statement: The recognized strong-endotactic condition of the positive lift is in coNP for the same sparse rational input model. Its extra condition is that every direction with a nonneutral edge has at least one inward edge at the maximum source score over all channels, including neutral channels; weak endotacticity is also required.
assumptions: Strong endotacticity uses the standard all-reactant source maximum
The sparse positive rational lift identity C8-RAT-1 holds
The reaction diagram has finitely many labeled channels
claims.novelty_boundary: No coNP-hardness lower bound for standard strong endotacticity is claimed. The weak 3SAT reduction does not transfer: the all-clauses UNSAT instance fails standard strong endotacticity in direction (0,0,0,-1) because neutral guard sources are global maximizers.
claims.costs: A strong counterdirection is a rational point satisfying finitely many piecewise-linear support, score-order, and neutral-sign relations; the exact solver may require exponential internal work.
claims.falsifier: A standard-strong counterdirection without an inward global all-source maximizer that has no rational direction witness, or a neutral source at the global maximum mishandled by the implementation.
claims.next_gate: Prove or refute coNP-hardness for standard strong endotacticity on this rational-rate interface, and independently compare the implementation against the GMS definition.

claims.statement: recognize_sparse_rational.py decides ordinary endotacticity or standard strong endotacticity through compact exact QF-LRA formulas without explicitly expanding denominator products. SAT directions are checked by a separate Fraction-based counterdirection verifier; solver timeout, resource limit, unavailable solver, or interrupted query returns UNKNOWN.
assumptions: Z3 Python solver supports exact rational linear arithmetic with ITE
The network JSON satisfies the stated finite sparse-support schema
REFUTED counterdirections pass the independent standard-library Fraction checker
claims.novelty_boundary: This is an implementation of the internal theorem/formula, not an externally validated solver, proof-checked UNSAT certificate, or claim of polynomial worst-case runtime.
claims.costs: One exact SMT query per candidate outward channel, and one further query for standard strong endotacticity after ordinary endotacticity passes. Formula size is polynomial in dimensions, channels, and sparse term count; Z3 internal runtime is exponential in the worst case, consistent with coNP-completeness. Input acquisition, coefficient positivity, exponent/jump bit lengths, solver memory, time, and resource limits are charged.
claims.falsifier: A REFUTED direction that fails exact independent Fraction replay, a false CERTIFIED answer on a known counterexample, incorrect neutral/global-top handling, or an UNKNOWN path mislabeled as a completed answer.
claims.next_gate: Add proof-object replay or an independently audited exact SMT backend; benchmark against materialized lifted-graph MILP on held-out fixed-dimension Hill/MM fixtures.

claims.statement: If the all-endotactic N33 permanence candidate is valid, a positive rational-rate system with a common strictly positive bounded measurable multiplier box and endotactic lifted support has the same conditional permanence consequence after the positive common-clock change. The corresponding strong-endotactic subfamily can instead be compared with the established GMS strong-endotactic permanence theorem, subject to its confined-system hypotheses.
assumptions: Every denominator is strictly positive on the positive orthant
There are finitely many channels and denominator supports
The original multipliers satisfy 0<kappa_min<=kappa_e(t)<=kappa_max<infinity
The lifted rates are measurable and lie in a common compact positive interval
The lifted trajectories enter a compact positive absorber before inverse-clock continuation is invoked
N33 is treated as conditional until externally verified
claims.novelty_boundary: The algebraic clock transfer is conditional on N33 for general endotactic systems. Strongly endotactic permanence is prior art. No all-dimensional general rational-rate permanence theorem is asserted here.
claims.costs: Explicit lift size may be exponential. The common clock D(x) is positive; its lower bound on the post-entry compact set exists but is not computed by this recognition program. Parameter acquisition, complete channel inventory, and rate-box validation are unperformed.
claims.falsifier: A violation of the common-height identity, failure of the finite lifted coefficients to share positive lower/upper bounds, or a clock that fails to tend to infinite original time after entry into the claimed compact positive set.
claims.next_gate: Independent external review of the N33 affine activity/weighted-drift proof; verify the exact lifted ODE interface and common-clock regularity for any named biochemical model.

claims.statement: For fixed direction/species dimension d, a central arrangement of reaction hyperplanes and within-support exponent-comparison hyperplanes has H^{O(d)} realizable faces; on each face all active signs and support maximizers are fixed, so exact rational LP feasibility decides whether an outward active top-tied witness exists. This is XP in d, not an FPT result.
assumptions: Explicit finite rational supports and rational reaction vectors
Exact ties are checked with weak top-score inequalities
All branch constraints are homogeneous, so a unit margin exactly models open-face strict signs
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a direct arrangement-complexity argument; no parameterized lower bound or FPT algorithm is established.
claims.costs: H is at most m plus the total number of within-support pairs; the face count is H^{O(d)} and each LP has polynomial encoding size. The bound is polynomial only for fixed d.
claims.falsifier: A realizable arrangement face on which support-maximizer or reaction-sign status is not fixed, or a counterdirection missed by the per-face LP conditions.
claims.next_gate: Implement and independently verify an exact low-dimensional face enumerator; compare it against the direct QF-LRA backend on randomized fixed-d inputs.
